title: Sinner, Rouse Thee from Thy Sleep
description: Sinner, Rouse Thee from Thy Sleep in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 268 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Sinner entreated to awake”, where the book credits them to the Episcopal Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sin-ner, rouse thee from thy sleep; Wake, and o'er thy fol-ly weep; Raise thy spir-it, dark and dead; Je-sus waits his light to shed.

lines: Sinner, rouse thee from thy sleep;
Wake, and o'er thy folly weep;
Raise thy spirit, dark and dead;
Jesus waits his light to shed.
Wake from sleep; arise from death;
See the bright and living path;
Watchful, tread that path; be wise;
Leave thy folly; seek the skies.
Leave thy folly; cease from crime;
From this hour redeem thy time;
Brief is this thy mortal day.
O, then, rouse thee from thy sleep;
Wake, and o'er thy folly weep;
Jesus calls from death and night;
Jesus waits to shed his light.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
